question: What is the difference between a stack and a queue? What do push, pop and peek do on a stack? Which of the two would you use for an editor's undo feature, and which for a line of print jobs waiting for a printer?
model_answer: A stack is last-in, first-out: you push and pop at the same end (the top), so the most recently added item comes out first. A queue is first-in, first-out: items join at the back and leave from the front, so the oldest item is served first. On a stack, push adds an item on top, pop removes and returns the top item, and peek only looks at the top without removing it. Undo must reverse the most recent action first, so it uses a stack; print jobs should be printed in arrival order, so they use a queue.
